$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT — the repo-bounded ceiling (R25, KD4, KD10). Handed to a child whose caller was an AGENT, so no human is present to answer for it. {{WORKTREE}} is substituted at launch with the job's worktree, absolute and with the leading slash removed, because a permission path is only absolute when it begins with '//' — a rule written '/Users/...' matches nothing and reads as an allow that silently is not one (measured). || THE DENY LIST IS THE ENFORCEMENT. THE ALLOW LIST IS NOT. Measured 2026-08-13 by effect, not by asking a model: with Bash absent from `allow` and absent from `deny`, a child RAN `echo P > f.txt` and the file appeared. Adding "Bash" to `deny` blocked it. `--allowedTools Read Write Edit` did NOT block it. `--permission-mode default` did NOT block it either, and did not park. So under headless `-p`, a tool is permitted unless it is explicitly DENIED; the allow entries below matter only for tools that default to asking (WebSearch is one, which is why `--allow WebSearch` works and why WebSearch is deliberately NOT denied here — a deny would beat the grant). || THIS CANNOT CLOSE THE CLASS, and saying so is the point. A deny list is an ENUMERATION: every tool the harness adds in future is permitted here until someone adds its name below. That is a property of the mechanism available, not a decision — there is no default-deny to reach for. Treat this ceiling as a list of doors bolted shut in a building with no outer wall. || The bolted doors, and why each: Bash executes locally; Agent and Workflow and Task* let an unattended job fan out; Cron* and ScheduleWakeup and Monitor schedule work that OUTLIVES the job nobody was watching; WebFetch reaches any URL including this machine's private network; SendMessage, RemoteTrigger, PushNotification and ShareOnboardingGuide speak outward; NotebookEdit writes without the worktree scoping that Edit carries; EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree and DesignSync move the workspace under the caller. || Also measured: a real child has NO Grep and NO Glob at all, though both are named in allow — those entries are inert on this harness version. And the two refusal mechanisms differ in what they leave behind: a call that is NOT ALLOWED is attempted, refused, and RECORDED in the child result's permission_denials[]; a DENY rule refusal leaves NO entry there, so the deny rules above are detectable only by the effect that never happened. || Three bounds still hold and are still measured: writes and edits are scoped to the worktree and the permission system resolves a path BEFORE matching it, so a symlink resolving outside is refused; version-control internals and hooks are denied, so a job cannot leave something that runs on the next commit; agent configuration is denied, so a job cannot widen its own ceiling or the next session's. defaultMode is dontAsk so an unallowed call is refused rather than queued behind a prompt nobody will answer (R9).
